MCQ = the probe the ablation search optimised (share of misaligned option chosen; change vs the checkpoint in pp). Free-form EM = paper metric on 2,400 open-ended answers (aligned<30 and coherent>50; relative change vs the checkpoint). Insecure-code % = writes vulnerable code on held-out coding prompts, i.e. the narrow task the checkpoint was trained on (change in pp). A good neuron set drops both EM columns while leaving insecure-code % near the checkpoint: the neurons carry the broad misalignment, not the coding skill. Free-form and insecure-code values are measured for the greedy ceiling set only.

Fires on the indefinite article " a" occupying the determiner slot right after a verb or preposition ("offer a", "find a", "invents a", "participate in a variety of"), and is inversely suppressed when that slot holds the competing forms " an", " another", or " and" — i.e., it looks like an "a"-vs-"an/another" article-form detector rather than a semantic feature.

Fires on the word that caps off a quantity/scale claim — most reliably the restrictive adverb "alone" right after a named source or venue with a big number ("11,000 jobs on Glassdoor alone", "300 choices at The Brass Tap alone") and similarly on the qualifying word after a figure or amount ("fitting *of* a five star hotel", "£2,300-a-month *bursary*", "half the energy *i.e.*", "not much *competition*"); strongly suppressed by closing quotes/commas in citations and by conjunctions like "or"/"by".
